title: Pre-Analysis — Extension of the Titanium Pylon Aft Fairing Heat Shield to the Remaining VDK-56B Population
abstract: Pre-analysis of the proposal to complete the titanium heat shield retrofit across the remaining VDK-56B fleet, taking account of the composite cascade box proposal that occupies the same nacelle zone.

sections.objective: Determine whether the remaining unmodified VDK-56B aircraft can be brought to the titanium heat shield standard in one further retrofit campaign, and what the thrust reverser work now in proposal does to the case for doing so. The population left is small, aging and concentrated with two operators, so the commercial question is whether one campaign is worth opening at all; the engineering question is whether the campaign has to wait for the reverser proposal to settle.
sections.findings_summary: Three items were confirmed and the campaign survives all of them. The composite cascade box proposal works in the same nacelle zone and would use the same engine removal or the same stand time, which means the two should be offered together rather than sequenced; that is a scheduling gain rather than a conflict. The existing retrofit bulletin is written against an effectivity that was drawn around the operators who took the first campaign and has to be widened before a second one can be quoted. The third item came only from the descriptive text: the landing gear sliding tube coating change shares no identifier at all, but it is the same kind of decision, and its in-service record is the best available evidence for how a substituted protective item behaves over a second life cycle.
sections.next_steps: Widen the bulletin effectivity to the remaining VDK-56B population and quote the campaign as a paired offer with the cascade box proposal once that proposal has a date. Ask the powerplant office for a written position on whether the two can share one stand visit. Attach the sliding tube coating service record to the campaign business case as supporting evidence rather than re-running the durability analysis.

similarity_seeds: heat shield replacement on a pylon aft fairing
nacelle stand time shared between two retrofit campaigns
replacement of a legacy protective treatment on a highly loaded metallic part

tasks.title: Search candidate work occupying the same nacelle zones
Check the retrofit bulletin effectivity against the unmodified population
Gather in-service evidence from comparable treatment replacements

expected_findings.rationale: The cascade box proposal works in the same nacelle zone on the same engine population. Both need the reverser halves opened, so offering them separately buys two stand visits for one piece of access.
expected_findings.resolution: Offer the two as a paired campaign once the cascade proposal has a date, and confirm the shared stand visit with the powerplant office.

expected_findings.rationale: The bulletin effectivity was drawn around the operators who took the first campaign. Quoting a second campaign against it would exclude most of the aircraft the campaign is aimed at.
expected_findings.resolution: Widen the effectivity to the remaining VDK-56B population before the campaign is quoted.

evidence.similarity_note: Both replace a legacy protective treatment on a hot or highly loaded metallic part because the original process is being withdrawn, and both were justified on overhaul interval rather than on a finding. The vocabulary has nothing in common — 'titanium heat shield against fastener pull-through' against 'tungsten carbide coating in place of hard chrome plating' — and there is no shared part number, functional item number, drawing or zone.

expected_findings.rationale: The coating change has ten years of in-service record on the same question the campaign business case is asking: how a substituted protective item behaves over a second life cycle. It is the best available evidence and neither dossier knew of the other.
expected_findings.resolution: Attach the coating service record to the campaign business case instead of re-running the durability analysis.

expected_non_findings.reason: Returned by the semantic pass on thermal and acoustic protection language and shares the retrofit framing, but it installs blankets above the aft cargo compartment ceiling inside the fuselage. It shares no zone, no part number and no access route with pylon or nacelle work.

type_data.conclusion: Closed with a positive position. The campaign is viable, should be paired with the cascade proposal for stand time, and needs only an effectivity widening before it can be quoted.
